subject: government-funding
story_title: The House sent a stopgap funding bill to the president, 370 to 48; he signed it the next day

sub_events.label: President signs H.R. 6500 as Public Law 119-103

records.title: Enrolled text of H.R. 6500, Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027
records.quote: December 11, 2026
records.about: The enrolled act that funds most agencies at fiscal year 2026 rates through December 11, 2026.

records.title: House roll call 286 on H.R. 6500
records.publisher: Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives
records.quote: AGOA Extension Act
records.about: The Clerk's electronic roll call: 370 to 48, party split, two-thirds required, still titled AGOA Extension Act.

records.title: Senate roll call vote 228 on H.R. 6500
records.quote: Bill Passed (90-6, 3/5 majority required)
records.about: The Senate's 3:37 a.m. August 8 vote passing the rewritten stopgap 90 to 6.

records.title: White House note that H.R. 6500 was signed
records.quote: On Wednesday, September 2, 2026, the President signed into law:
records.about: The White House record of the September 2 signature, naming the act and the December 11 date.

records.title: Statement of Administration Policy on the Senate amendment to H.R. 6500
records.quote: The Administration supports the Senate Amendment to H.R. 6500.
records.about: The August 3 policy paper recommending a signature if the Senate text reached the president.

records.title: Speaker Johnson remarks after the House stopgap vote
records.quote: Thanks to the House Republicans
records.about: The Speaker's September 1 remarks after the House passed the stopgap.

records.title: Chairman Cole floor remarks on the Senate amendments to H.R. 6500
records.quote: certainty that the government will remain open
records.about: Cole's floor speech listing who stays paid or served under the stopgap.

records.title: House Appropriations release on sending H.R. 6500 to the president
records.quote: The measure was approved by a vote of 370
records.about: The committee's written statement after the 370-48 vote.

records.title: DeLauro statement on House passage of the continuing resolution
records.quote: We have 101 days until government funding expires
records.about: The ranking member's statement counting 101 days to December 11 and calling for the twelve bills.

records.title: Collins statement on House passage of the continuing resolution
records.quote: which would politicize the grant process
records.about: The Senate Appropriations chair's statement after the House vote, including the grants-rule delay.

records.title: Murray statement on Senate passage of the continuing resolution
records.quote: It closes the loophole that would have allowed the Trump administration to transfer funding for other programs to Border Patrol.
records.about: The vice chair's August 8 statement describing Senate additions, including the Border Patrol transfer claim.

records.title: House passes funding bill, avoiding shutdown ahead of midterm elections
records.quote: By a count of 370 to 48
records.about: ABC's September 1 article on the House vote, the 19-29 opposition split, and the August 8 Senate passage.

records.title: House passes short-term funding bill to avoid shutdown
records.quote: The House passed the bill by a vote of 370-48
records.about: The Associated Press dispatch on the House vote, Cole's certainty line, and DeLauro's closed-door remarks.

records.title: Congress funds government until December, averting preelection shutdown
records.quote: passed the House on a 370-48 vote
records.about: The Hill's September 1 article, including the hemp-ban characterization and the grants rule.

records.title: Congress passes funding bill to avoid shutdown before midterms
records.quote: passed the measure in a 370 to 48 vote
records.about: CBS's September 1 article on the two-thirds vote and the December 11 date.

records.title: House passes short-term funding bill to prevent a shutdown before the election
records.quote: sailed through the chamber by a vote of 370-48
records.about: NBC's September 1 article, including Cole on finishing the twelve bills after the election.

records.title: Congress averts a government shutdown ahead of the midterms
records.quote: The legislation passed the House 370-48 with bipartisan support
records.about: NPR's September 1 article on current levels with exceptions and White House encouragement.

records.title: House passes short-term spending bill, staving off another fund fight during midterms
records.quote: The House passed the bill by a vote of 370-48
records.about: PBS NewsHour's posting of the Associated Press dispatch.

records.title: House votes to fund government through Dec. 11, avert shutdown before midterms
records.quote: Twenty-nine Democrats and 19 Republicans voted against it
records.about: UPI's September 1 article with the 29-Democrat and 19-Republican opposition split.

records.title: Trump signs stopgap funding bill into law, temporarily avoiding shutdown
records.quote: President Trump on Wednesday signed a stopgap government funding bill into law
records.about: The Hill's September 2 article on the signature, restating the two roll-call margins.

records.title: Senate roll call vote 227, motion to table Budd amendment 6747
records.quote: Motion to Table Agreed to (61-32)
records.about: The 2:36 a.m. August 8 vote tabling Senator Budd's amendment 6747, 61 to 32.

records.title: House roll call 288 on H. Res. 1499
records.publisher: Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives
records.quote: On Agreeing to the Resolution
records.about: The 210-208 rule vote the same afternoon as the stopgap, with five Republican nays and two Democratic yeas.
